submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 with a threshold of 35 GeV achieves the highest signal efficiency of 93.878% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This represents approximately 9% higher efficiency than Algorithm-L2 (84.547% at 35 GeV) and 20% higher than Algorithm-L3 (73.896% at 35 GeV). Systematic scanning of thresholds from 20 to 50 GeV confirmed that 35 GeV is the optimal operating point for Algorithm-L1, balancing signal acceptance against the rate constraint. The iterative topological clustering with learned calibration (Algorithm-L1) provides superior performance compared to the sliding-window (Algorithm-L2) and fixed-window approaches (Algorithm-L3), likely due to better reconstruction of the signal topology and more accurate energy calibration.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 at 35 GeV achieves 93.878% signal efficiency, the highest among all tested configurations. This was verified through systematic scans across all three algorithms and threshold range 20-60 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) is explicitly listed as one of the three candidate algorithms in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md states that all three algorithms 'fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs)', confirming Algorithm-L1 can be deployed in Level-1 trigger hardware.
The recommended threshold of 35 GeV falls within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.
